# Capability reference

Every capability id `capability.py` answers for, and what it becomes.
Generated from the mapping, so it cannot drift from it; the script's
docstring says how to regenerate.

An entry reads `name · type · diag · off`: the entity name, which is
also its translation key; the mapping type, which decides the platform
that builds the entity; whether it lands in the diagnostic category;
and whether it arrives switched off in the entity registry.

172 ids in total. Names and types here are what the mapping
claims, not what has been verified against hardware -- most of the
table came from one user's capture of one device.

## The 24 self-describing ids

Named from the vendor's own capability list, which gives an identifier
and nothing else -- no unit, no encoding, no way to read a bitmask. They
are surfaced as raw strings and arrive switched off, so they cost
nothing until someone turns one on to investigate it. They appear in the
tables above like any other id.
